ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and beneficial owners against the Taiwan Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau (MJIB) money laundering prevention database, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Consolidated List, the EU and UK HMT financial sanctions lists, and the PRC sanctions list. For cross-strait operations, additional enhanced due diligence is required for any Taiwan or China public officials, and the firm must maintain a risk-based transaction monitoring system for success-fee wires and SWIFT transfers involving M&A advisory services, including adverse media checks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce - Company Name and Business Scope Reservation Application System (Taiwan Company Registration Online Platform)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be in traditional Chinese; an English name may be registered solely as a secondary transliteration of the Chinese name. The four-tier naming convention requires [Taiwan] + [specific trade name] + [business type] + [limited company]. Pinyin without Chinese characters is prohibited; all legal filings, notices, and invoices must refer to the Chinese name. The English name must exactly correspond to the Chinese name and be recorded in the registry after the Chinese name approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name reservation is rejected, the applicant must first correct any conflicts by filing a new prereview application or submit a written objection to the Commerce Department within 30 days from the rejection date. The department will re-issue a rejection or approval within 15 working days. A formal administrative appeal can be lodged with the Executive Yuan (appeal commission) within 30 days of the re-rejection, and if that fails, administrative litigation may be commenced in the Taipei High Administrative Court. All appeals must be submitted through the online platform with a notarized authorization.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox addresses are legally registrable in Taiwan for low-risk entities, but the National Taxation Bureau and most corporate banks reject them for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced M&A advisory boutique. A physical office with a dedicated reception, lease for at least 12 months, utility bills, and evidence of local management presence is required for obtaining the unified business invoice number, opening corporate bank accounts, and satisfying AML/CFT entity due diligence. Use of a virtual office alone will likely trigger enhanced examination and business license revocation risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced on-site inspections are moderately likely (estimated 35% risk in the first fiscal year) given the M&A advisory classification and cross-strait capital flows. Checklist: 1) Verify lease original and rent receipts; 2) Confirm placement of outdoor business signage; 3) Audit employees' attendance and payroll; 4) Check desks, computers, filing cabinets, and wiring; 5) Interview the responsible person on business scope; 6) Examine client engagement letters and invoice book; 7) Confirm the presence of the registered responsible person or authorised manager.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 23, 24, 27, 29, 32, 33, 38, 47 and 53; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 5, 28, 29 and 31-33; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Decree No. 746), Articles 2 and 8-22; and the negative-list provisions of the Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (2021), read together with the Regulations on the Administration of Investment by Taiwan Compatriots because the sole investor is domiciled in Taiwan.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - Enterprise Registration Bureau; the local municipal or district Market Regulation Administration with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office in mainland China; foreign investment information is filed to the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the integrated Foreign Investment Information Reporting system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Market Entity Registration Application Form (Gongsi Dengji Shenqingshu) submitted together with the Articles of Association, the pre-approved name notice, the registered office lease and supporting incorporation docket, through the national or provincial one-stop enterprise opening online platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under PRC law. The subscribed capital must be fully paid in by the shareholder within five years of registration under Company Law Article 47, unless a shorter period is required by a specific industry regulator. There is no blocked escrow account rule; instead, foreign capital from Taiwan must be remitted through an FDI capital account at a PBOC-designated bank, and the company must maintain the inward capital verification record. The Taiwan investor may contribute in USD or CNY-equivalent, and the contributed capital cannot be used for unauthorized equity investments or restricted activities outside the approved business scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) via the provincial Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal; for any Taiwan-side taxable nexus, the Ministry of Finance, R.O.C. and the National Taxation Bureau are the competent counterpart authorities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the CN WFOE: (1) incorporate with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC); (2) complete tax registration through the STA's one-stop data sharing process within 30 days after issuance of the business license, with the USCC serving as the de facto tax identification number; (3) file the foreign investment information report through SAMR and complete SAFE-designated bank foreign exchange registration for capital and dividend remittances; (4) apply for VAT general taxpayer status when annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000, while a below-threshold WFOE may be treated as a small-scale taxpayer with a simplified collection rate; (5) for a non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in China, a withholding registration is still required for China-source income; for a Taiwan-side branch or permanent establishment, registration with the Ministry of Finance, R.O.C. is required to obtain a Taiwan Uniform Invoice Number and a tax file reference.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; China does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. A WFOE is per se a resident limited-liability enterprise taxed at entity level under Corporate Income Tax, and hybrid mismatch or treaty-based classification choices are not available as elective domestic classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for mandatory tax registration; every legal entity must obtain VAT registration within 30 days of business registration. Mandatory general taxpayer registration threshold is annual VAT taxable sales above RMB 5,000,000; below this threshold the WFOE is a small-scale taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Golden Tax IV mandate: all Special VAT Invoices and fully digitalized electronic invoices must be issued through the STA electronic invoice platform, reported in real time to the national VAT invoice database, and contain a cryptographically verifiable unique invoice number and QR-based digital stamping. ERP-to-platform API integration is required for all automated billing environments; paper-only issuance is reserved for narrow statutory transition cases.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported physical goods qualify for 0% VAT when they are actually exported through customs with an export customs declaration and the seller is a VAT general taxpayer holding the full statutory export document set. Cross-border services qualify for zero-rating only if listed in the PRC cross-border taxable services catalogue (e.g., R&D, design, software, data processing, offshore outsourcing, international transportation, and similar specified services); M&A and management consulting services wholly consumed offshore are generally VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated, meaning no output VAT is charged but input VAT may not be refunded unless the service specifically falls into a zero-rated catalogue item. The recipient must be outside mainland China and the service must be wholly consumed outside China, with contemporaneous foreign currency receipts substantiating the offshore character.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry / China export customs declaration) with customs release notation
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from China
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign-exchange receipt voucher from a SAFE-licensed bank
Signed export contract, commercial invoice, packing list, and any restricted-goods export licenses
VAT export tax refund declaration and electronic document matching with the STA tax and customs systems
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False export declarations, inflated export values, fabricated offshore service contracts, or missing FX repatriation within the 180-day window trigger retrospective clawback of zero-rated VAT treatment, repayment of output VAT, and late-payment interest. Under the PRC Tax Administration and Collection Law, fraudulent export tax recovery is punishable by recovery of the full amount and a fine of up to three times the tax evaded; severe cases are prosecuted as criminal export tax rebate fraud under PRC Criminal Law, with imprisonment, fines, and asset confiscation. Regulatory non-compliance with SAFE reporting may independently subject the entity to foreign-exchange penalties and disqualify the export zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, the foreign exchange administration authority operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC), with local SAFE branches administering cross-border capital registration, FX market supervision, and balance of payments reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China operates an essentially convertible current account and a heavily managed capital account. Current account FX receipts and payments for trade in goods and services may be transacted freely through designated banks if evidenced by contracts, invoices, customs declarations, and tax vouchers, under the real intention and real transaction background principles. Export proceeds are not subject to a mandatory surrender ratio and may be retained in foreign currency accounts or converted at the market rate through a designated bank. Capital account flows, including FDI equity injection, shareholder loans, establishment of escrow capital, and cross-border M&A funding, are subject to pre-approval, filing, and post-monitoring by SAFE. For the WFOE, the registered foreign exchange capital can be converted and used only within the approved business scope and the negative list framework. M&A success fee inflows are classified as service trade current account receipts and are remittable after contract verification, tax payment, and bank-level SAFE reporting. Dividend remittances to the Taiwan investor are allowed after the annual statutory audit, tax settlement, and SAFE reporting, but require evidence of bookkeeping accuracy, tax clearance, and absence of historical false declarations. The New Taiwan Dollar is not an onshore deliverable currency in mainland China, so all funding from Taiwan should be wired in USD or RMB via SWIFT or CIPS.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE monitoring rules, an exporter must repatriate export proceeds to a domestic foreign exchange account within 180 days from the date of customs declaration unless an extension is approved by SAFE. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the WFOE may either retain the foreign exchange in a current account or sell it to a designated bank at the prevailing market rate. Any conversion must be supported by the export cargo declaration, logistics documents, invoice, and the SAFE trade-inspection code. For cross-border service exports such as M&A advisory fees, the applicable 180-day collection requirement is enforced through the service trade item, with bank-level declaration submitted via the SAFE system and retained with the underlying advisory contract.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary or sole treasury rail. Under the Administrative Measures for Non-bank Payment Institutions and SAFE foreign exchange regulations, a foreign fintech EMI cannot open onshore deposit-taking accounts, accept FDI capital injections, or execute SAFE-registered FX settlement without a PBOC payment license and cross-border payment institution designation. Offshore EMIs such as Airwallex, Currenxie, or Wise may only serve as auxiliary collection tools in partnership with licensed Chinese banks and cannot replace the bank for capital account transactions. For a WFOE engaged in M&A advisory, all core treasury clearing should be executed through licensed banks; fintech EMIs are viable only for small-volume, low-value service fee collections and only if the bank has previously cleared the counterparty and the underlying transaction documentation is retained.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted in Mainland China for a newly formed WFOE. The bank will require the WFOE's legal representative and the Taiwan investor's authorized signatory to appear in person at least once for the initial account opening and enhanced due diligence interview. If a Taiwan statutory director cannot travel, a notarized power of attorney authenticated by the Taiwan notary system and the Straits Exchange Foundation may permit the WFOE's local finance director to act as the KYC contact, but the bank reserves the right to require a live video conference with the Taiwan principal. After the inaugural physical interview, routine operations may be conducted online via corporate internet banking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directorship and ultimate beneficial owner identity ambiguity for the Taiwan investor, with an unverifiable natural person chain behind the Taiwan corporate shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Taiwan investing entity's business registration dossier from the Ministry of Economic Affairs, audited financial statements for the last three years, bank statements evidencing the source of investment funds, a shareholder register traced to natural persons, a notarized Certificate of Incumbency, and an independent UBO opinion letter from a licensed compliance firm in Taiwan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing cross-strait investment approval and SAFE FDI registration, causing the bank to suspect that the WFOE is unlicensed or operating outside the foreign-invested enterprise framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the WFOE's business license with the Taiwanese investment annotation, the filing receipt or approval certificate for the Taiwan investment enterprise issued by the local commerce department and Taiwan Affairs Office, the SAFE Foreign Investment FDI Registration Form establishing the compliance code, and the national enterprise credit information report confirming the legal establishment and operating status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: M&A advisory success fee inflows display high turnover velocity and complex fee splitting with no clear contractual basis, creating trade-based money laundering and structuring red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver executed engagement letters and advisory agreements for each transaction, board resolutions approving fee structures, milestone invoices with full fee calculation formulas, deal progress documentation including correspondence and closing minutes, and audited bank statements of the receiving account; supplement with an explanation of the economic substance of every fee movement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and politically exposed persons exposure of Taiwan deal counterparties or shareholders, particularly where payments may transit restricted industries or high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a live sanctions and PEP screening report on all shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners from a recognized screening provider, a corporate due diligence report on each counterparty, anti-bribery and anti-money laundering compliance policies, self-declarations confirming no connection to sanctioned parties, and a written commitment to freeze any funds attributable to sanctioned jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan investor converts New Taiwan Dollars to USD or RMB and executes a cross-border wire via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's FDI capital escrow account at a designated licensed bank. Before the transfer, the WFOE must complete SAFE foreign exchange registration for the foreign-invested enterprise and obtain the FDI compliance registration certificate. The remittance instruction must identify the SAFE registration code and use the SAFE purpose code category for FDI paid-in capital injection. Upon receipt, the receiving bank verifies the SAFE registration, credits the capital account, and settles the foreign exchange into RMB under the real need principle. The WFOE then engages a Chinese certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report, and all downstream disbursements must be matched against business contracts, vouchers, and the approved business scope. Any transfer of escrowed capital must not be commingled with operational income without proper account separation and bank approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border service trade expenditures related to M&A advisory work, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for USD or RMB wire transfers, accompanied by the appropriate service trade declaration code, tax withholding certificate, and underlying contract. For large or milestone-based payments, a Commercial Letter of Credit may be opened via SWIFT MT700 when the counterparty requires trade finance protection, although this is uncommon for advisory fees. Documentary Collections via SWIFT MT400 or MT422 can be used for time-gated deliverables linked to supporting documents. For RMB-denominated payments to Taiwan or other counterparties, the Cross-border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) provides an efficient alternative to SWIFT and reduces correspondent bank delays. Every outbound payment must be supported by a board resolution, invoice, contract, and a negative-list compliance check confirming the transaction is not a prohibited capital flight or money-laundering scheme.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forward contracts (remote and regular forwards) with licensed Chinese banks, executed only when the WFOE demonstrates genuine current or capital account exposure under SAFE real transaction background rules.

Onshore FX options and option combination structures such as risk reversals, collars, and participating forwards, limited to hedging existing or highly expected trade settlement flows and requiring bank credit approval.
Cross-currency swaps between RMB and USD for term-based corporate financing or M&A funding, subject to SAFE risk management accreditation and strict prohibition on speculative net positions.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are prohibited for the onshore WFOE as a hedging instrument because SAFE requires physical RMB delivery and a genuine underlying transaction; NDFs are only permissible for offshore non-resident counterparties transacting outside mainland China.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Report (Business Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually between January 1 and June 30 covering the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission places the WFOE on the Operation Abnormality List; non-filing for three consecutive years risks SAMR administrative strike-off; false declarations incur fines up to RMB 10,000 and adverse public credit records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) Annual Reconciliation Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) — competent local tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the year following the tax year, reconciling quarterly prepayments against audited annual results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of RMB 2,000–10,000; daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on underpaid EIT; enforced collection proceedings, transfer-pricing audits, and withholding tax scrutiny on dividend remittances to the Taiwanese parent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Financial Statements Audit and Certified Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed PRC CPA firm engaged by the WFOE; audited statements are submitted to the shareholders' meeting, the SAMR annual report and the tax reconciliation file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit completion must precede the April 30 tax-review reference date and the June 30 annual report deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitting the independent audit invalidates reliable annual reporting, triggers SAMR abnormal listing, supports shareholder or tax authority requests for compulsory audit, and heightens re-assessment risk for undeclared cross-border M&A advisory income.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR with mandatory data transmission to the Ministry of Commerce and Taiwan Affairs coordination bodies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed conjunctively with the NECIPS annual report from January 1 to June 30; re-filing required within 20 working days after any equity transfer or registered capital alteration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false reporting triggers a corrective order and fines of RMB 100,000–500,000 under Article 34 of the PRC Foreign Investment Law, together with an adverse national enterprise credit flag.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Stock Equity Registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the integrated SAMR/SAFE annual report system or the WFOE's designated foreign-exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before June 30, reporting year-end FDI stock equity and creditor balances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing or inaccurate registration constrains the WFOE's FX profit repatriation, shareholder loan repayment and SWIFT success-fee conversion; SAFE may impose fines and compel enhanced bank-level compliance review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and SAMR through the integrated Beneficial Ownership Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing at incorporation; updates due within 30 days of any share transfer; annual re-confirmation performed within the June 30 annual report window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, false or omitted UBO declarations attract PBOC administrative penalties of RMB 10,000–100,000 per violation, elevate the AML risk rating, and obstruct clearing of cross-border success-fee payments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cross-Strait Investment Annual Operating Status Declaration (filed by the Taiwan direct shareholder)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission (MOEAIC), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the end of May following the reporting calendar year; equity-change notifications required within six months of any shareholding transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing exposes the Taiwanese investor to MOEAIC administrative sanctions, suspension of further mainland China investment approvals, retroactive examination of the WFOE establishment approval, and penalties under cross-strait investment rules.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for every PRC limited liability company with no size-based exemption: the revised PRC Company Law (effective 1 July 2024) requires the WFOE to prepare annual financial statements and obtain an independent CPA audit every fiscal year irrespective of revenue, assets or headcount; the audit is also a statutory precondition to both the SAMR annual report and the EIT annual reconciliation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (PRC GAAP, substantially converged with IFRS); RMB is the statutory reporting currency and books are maintained in simplified Chinese.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: On every share transfer among existing shareholders, the WFOE updates the Register of Members on the same business day, files the equity change with SAMR within 30 days, and refreshes the UBO chain identifying every natural person holding 25% or more equity or exercising ultimate effective control; when no equity movement occurs, the registers and UBO chain are formally re-confirmed each year within the NECIPS annual report and the Beneficial Ownership Information System, certifying that no unreported ownership change exists.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Virtual registered office and mail handling: USD 150–600 per annum; full licensed corporate secretarial and annual compliance agency coverage in Beijing, Shanghai or Shenzhen: USD 400–1,800 per annum.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Independent CPA audit for a medium-sized WFOE: USD 1,500–6,000; a cross-border M&A advisory boutique with related-party success-fee flows, SWIFT receivables and intercompany balances is typically quoted USD 2,500–8,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% for qualifying encouraged industries in certain regions (e.g., Western China Development Program); small and low-profit enterprises taxed at 20% effective rate on taxable income up to RMB 3 million with additional progressive reductions; additional super deduction of 100% for qualifying R&D expenses; foreign-invested enterprises may also access preferential rates under special regional regimes such as Hainan Free Trade Port or Lingang New Area, subject to substantive business operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A10026 (中华人民共和国企业所得税年度纳税申报表, Annual Corporate Income Tax Return) submitted via the State Taxation Administration electronic filing system (e-Tax, 电子税务局) or through local tax bureau in-charge; quarterly provisional returns filed on Form A200000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly provisional filings and prepayments)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual CIT return must be filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (by 31 May for calendar-year taxpayers); quarterly prepayments due within 15 days after each quarter end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue from principal business (M&A advisory service fees and success fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report revenue derived from both domestic and cross-border advisory engagements in RMB; apply China-source income rules for services performed or utilized in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating cost: direct deal-team compensation, external research costs, IT infrastructure, and due-diligence subcontractor fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only costs supported by legally valid invoices (fapiao) and with clear business relevance are deductible; cross-border cost allocations must be arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling and marketing expenses: client development, business travel, deal-Origination costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Advertising and entertainment expenses are subject to statutory caps (60% of entertainment expense, capped at 0.5% of revenue); non-resident parent-originated marketing costs must be substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General and administrative expenses: office rent, professional fees, compliance, directors' costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocations from foreign head office are deductible only if in compliance with service transaction rules and supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income: foreign-exchange gains, penalty-free government grants, sundry income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-exchange gains are generally taxable; non-resident investors may owe withholding tax on passive income separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income after adjustments (accounting profit adjusted for tax-law differences).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure all intercompany charges are adjusted to arm's length; undeclared cross-border fees to affiliated offshore entities are a common audit target.
Enter 25% unless a preferential 15% or 20% effective rate applies based on qualified status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT payable before credits (taxable income × applicable rate).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offset quarterly prepayments already made to determine balance due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits (for foreign-source income taxes paid).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE may credit direct and indirect foreign taxes on foreign-source income, capped at the China CIT payable share.
Settle any balance with STA e-tax; overpayments can be refunded or applied forward.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: RMB 2,000–10,000 penalty (up to RMB 50,000 for aggravated cases) plus daily surcharge of 0.05% on unpaid tax for each day of delay; late payment: additional penalty of 50%–500% of underpaid tax if fraudulent underreporting or evasion is established.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (statutory) for dividends distributed by a Chinese resident enterprise to non-resident corporate shareholders; the rate may be reduced to 5% under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement (海峡两岸避免双重课税及加强税务合作协议) where the Taiwan-resident beneficial owner directly holds at least 25% of the capital and meets substantive conditions, subject to administrative approval.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim relief under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement or an applicable DTA, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Resident Certificate (TRC) from the Taiwan competent authority or relevant treaty jurisdiction; (2) complete and submit the DTA benefit application form (e.g., STA Form for Treaty Benefits) to the Chinese payer or in-charge tax bureau before or at the time of dividend distribution; (3) provide documentary evidence of beneficial ownership, direct shareholding, substance, and absence of conduit arrangements; (4) receive a written approval or reduced-withholding notice from the tax authority; without pre-approval or TRC, the statutory 10% rate applies and no retroactive refund is guaranteed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rate for royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 10%. Under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, reduced rates may apply (generally 7.5% for royalties and 7.5% for interest) depending on beneficial ownership and approval; without a valid treaty benefit claim, the statutory 10% rate is withheld. For royalties, the payer must also examine the deductibility conditions and VAT/service tax implications.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File preparation under STA Bulletin [2016] No. 42 is triggered when annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 100 million for a single type or RMB 40 million for multiple transaction types; a contemporaneous transfer pricing report must be prepared above thresholds; lower threshold applies for related-party intangible property or financial transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies the substance-over-form doctrine and General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR) under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. A WFOE M&A advisory boutique must maintain real economic substance in China—employees, office premises, decision-making, execution of core advisory functions, and risk management. The Cross-Strait Tax Agreement benefits are denied if the Taiwan entity is deemed a conduit without substantive business activity. Any arrangement solely to obtain treaty benefits may be recharacterized, and the Chinese entity could be subject to deemed distributions, additional CIT, and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fabricating fake fapiao (invoices) to inflate deductions; underreporting success fees received via offshore accounts; deliberately omitting China-source advisory income from CIT returns; or using shell entities to siphon profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of tax exemptions, additional tax assessment, daily interest of 0.05%, administrative fine of 50% up to 500% of the underpaid tax; criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201 for evading tax exceeding RMB 50,000 with imprisonment up to 7 years and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the unpaid tax if the corporate veil is pierced due to fraud or abuse of corporate form; travel bans and exit-control orders can be imposed; personal assets may be frozen for restitution; imprisonment for the legal representative and directly responsible supervisors is possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Taiwan or offshore intermediate company with little or no economic substance solely to reduce dividend/royalty withholding under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement or a third-country DTA; or receiving M&A advisory fees in a zero-tax jurisdiction while the actual management, personnel, and deal execution occur in mainland China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of the transaction, full statutory withholding of 10% (or 25% CIT on service income deemed received by a permanent establishment), plus late payment interest and 50%–500% penalties; GAAR reassessment with unlimited look-back period for tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders and directors of the WFOE and the offshore intermediary can be held jointly and severally liable for tax, interest, and penalties; travel restrictions and freezing of bank accounts are commonly enforced during cross-border tax investigations; criminal liability for organizing a tax-evasion scheme may lead to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting success fees in cash, failing to perform client due diligence for cross-border M&A deals, using layered wire transfers through jurisdictions with weak AML controls to obscure the origin or destination of funds, or processing transactions for sanctioned/ politically exposed clients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines on the company up to RMB 5 million; suspension or revocation of licenses; asset forfeiture; criminal liability under China's Anti-Money Laundering Law for money laundering with imprisonment up to 10 years; inclusion on the financial blacklist.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers must personally ensure AML controls; penalties include fines, travel bans, custodial detention, and criminal imprisonment for willful blindness; personal assets can be traced and confiscated if complicity is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing brokerage, deal-structuring, valuation, or securities-related M&A advice without holding required licenses from the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) for outbound M&A, or other financial authorities; conducting cross-border M&A advisory in China without approval.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cease-and-desist order, confiscation of illegal gains, administrative fine of RMB 100,000–1,000,000 (or 1–5 times the illegal income); criminal prosecution for illegal business operations (非法经营罪) with imprisonment up to 5–10 years and property confiscation; invalidation of advisory contracts and no right to collect success fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the actual controller are subject to personal fines and imprisonment; regulatory authorities can impose industry bans and travel restrictions; clients may sue for restitution, and courts may pierce the corporate veil to satisfy judgments from personal assets.
